distractors.reason: We don't say 'very booked'. 'Very' intensifies ordinary qualities (very busy, very late), but not 'booked' in this sense.
We don't say 'deeply booked'. 'Deeply' is used with feelings and emotions (deeply concerned, deeply sorry).
We don't say 'highly booked'. 'Highly' is used with positive or important qualities (highly recommended, highly skilled).

example_sentence: My schedule is ___ booked on Monday.
l1_interference: Los hispanohablantes suelen usar 'very' para casi todo y por eso dicen 'very booked' en vez de 'fully booked'. Conviene recordar que 'fully' indica que algo está completo.
explanation: In English, 'fully' means completely or totally full. We use it with 'booked', 'packed', 'occupied' and 'ready' to show that there is no space or time left.

related_collocations.example: I am completely free on Saturday afternoon.
This week my schedule is totally busy.

memory_tip: FULLY = completely full or complete (booked, packed, ready) | VERY = a high degree of an ordinary quality (very busy, very late)
